reasoning_traces.think:
The core methodology combines ordinal logistic regression with historical data to predict tournament outcomes. Teams are characterized by regular-season metrics, which are mapped to ordinal win probabilities using cumulative logit models. These probabilities are then aggregated into expected win counts, forming a numerical rating that reflects team strength. This process enables the NCAA committee to assign seeds and regions while ensuring competitive balance. The framework assumes ordered categorical outcomes and uses maximum likelihood estimation to fit parameters. Failure modes include overfitting due to limited data, incorrect ordering of categories, or exclusion of relevant variables. The model must also satisfy marginal constraints—such as fixed numbers of teams advancing at each stage—to maintain realism. Dualities emerge between predictive accuracy and tournament fairness: high-rated teams should win more often, but randomness must be preserved to maintain excitement. The system operates under uncertainty, requiring robust calibration and validation against past results.
